answer.rationale: Write-path p99 degradation began shortly after a release 2 hours ago, making the release the leading suspect. Read-replica routing (b5) helps reads, not writes, and circuit breakers (b4) target dependency failures — neither fits. Failover (b2) doesn't address a bad build. Rollback (b1) is the intervention that previously cleared a latency/error regression without customer impact and directly protects in-flight customer writes; b6 supports that the gating process exists but this build reached GA. Peak settlement traffic raises the cost of waiting, and rollback is reversible if the release proves innocent. I verify b1 to confirm the rollback procedure completed cleanly before, since it is the action I am about to take. Residual uncertainty: the peak write load itself could be the cause, so I will watch latency post-rollback and fall back to add_capacity next window if it persists.
